tldr: OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Sol and Luna on Sep 22, an hour after Claude Opus 5.5, as vendors cut prices. A week later GPT-6.1 Sol arrived with near-Astra intelligence at one-fifth of Astra's API token prices.
whats_new: A secondary report says Codex CLI now defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol and cuts price 80%; the claim is unconfirmed by OpenAI in this thread.
why_it_matters: GPT-6.1 Sol lowers the price of Astra-class coding and computer-use work, so routing and cost-per-task assumptions built on Astra pricing are out of date.

status.detail: GPT-6.1 Sol has moved from launch to customer cost claims and a reported Codex CLI default.

GPT-6.1 Sol: near-Astra intelligence at one-fifth of Astra's token prices
beats.summary: OpenAI pitches it for coding, computer use and professional work.

open_questions: Does OpenAI confirm Codex CLI's default switch to GPT-6.1 Sol and the 80% price cut?
Does Asana's 76x cost reduction reproduce outside its browser-agent tests?
How does GPT-6.1 Sol compare with Claude Opus 5.5 on cost per completed task?
take_for_builders: Rerun your coding and computer-use evals on GPT-6.1 Sol against your current Astra baseline, comparing cost per completed task, before changing any default model.
